title: Pinches, lasers and other paths to fusion
description: From the pinches of the 1950s to laser ignition at NIF, spherical tokamaks, high-temperature superconducting magnets and private concepts: what each path has shown, what it still lacks, and how to tell results from claims.

sources.title: Z-pinch (Wikipedia): how it works, the kink instability, ZETA, Zap Energy (founded 2017)
Theta pinch (Wikipedia): Scylla I 1958, first clear evidence of thermonuclear fusion, end losses, Scyllac closed 1977
Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory: Achieving fusion ignition (shots of 5 Dec 2022 to 20 June 2026, how indirect drive works)
National Ignition Facility (Wikipedia): about 300 MJ of electricity for the 2.05 MJ pulse, about one shot every two days in 2014, weapons research
Spherical tokamak (Wikipedia): aspect ratio, START (January 1991, beta about 40 %), the central column
UKAEA: STEP programme (prototype spherical tokamak plant at West Burton, delivered by UK Industrial Fusion Solutions)
World Nuclear News, 1 November 2024: STEP due to operate by 2040, net electricity above 100 MW
MIT Energy Initiative: 20 tesla high-temperature superconducting magnet, 5 September 2021
SPARC (Wikipedia): Commonwealth Fusion Systems, Devens, 12.2 T, R = 1.85 m, planned first plasma 2027, expected Q about 11; 20 T at 20 K
Helion Energy (Wikipedia): field-reversed configurations, Microsoft agreement of 10 May 2023 for 2028, plant near Malaga, Washington (2025); no net electricity shown
General Fusion (Wikipedia): magnetized target fusion, LM26, about 25 % of staff cut in May 2025
Laser Mégajoule (Wikipedia): CEA laser facility near Bordeaux, operational 23 October 2014
ITER (Wikipedia): the 2024 baseline (research operation 2034, deuterium–tritium operation 2039)
Mega Ampere Spherical Tokamak (Wikipedia): MAST Upgrade at Culham, first plasma October 2020
